A.rule: Specific, attributable to the candidate personally, and quantified or with a verifiable outcome.

B.rule: Specific and attributable, but no number or outcome.

C.rule: Team-attributed ('part of', 'supported', 'assisted', 'we'), generic, or a claim with no context.

evidence_grades.grounding: Instincts anti-signal: 'every achievement framed as part of a large team, with no individual call visible'; non-signal: 'framework vocabulary describes method, not evidence of doing the work'.

evidence_validation.rule: Every criterion with level > 0 must have at least one evidence snippet that appears in the redacted CV text (normalised substring, or fuzzy ratio >= 0.85). If none matches, the level is forced to 0 and flag 'evidence_not_found:<id>' is raised.
evidence_validation.grounding: Protects against the model inventing experience; a ranking Arjun can defend must be traceable to the CV.

review.meaning: Arjun decides; no email drafted until he does.

not_shortlisted.meaning: Respectful rejection drafted; sent only on Arjun's click.

capacity.overflow_action: Demote lowest-ranked overflow to the next band with flag 'cleared_bar_capacity'.
capacity.grounding: Case: Arjun has no HR, is the hiring manager for every role, and reviews in 45-minute windows. Success is one offer, not a long list.

items.grounding: Instincts non-signal: certifications, community signals, LeetCode appear mainly in the non-thriving group.
Instincts anti-signal: domain knowledge described only through tools, APIs or customers, never through doing the work.
Instincts anti-signal: every achievement framed as part of a large team (the Below Expectations hire's pattern).

items.when: cv_style.framework_terms_count >= 4 AND NOT any killed/reversed/failure evidence
items.grounding: Instincts non-signal: framework vocabulary (JTBD, OKR, Agile) without concrete stories.
PM JD: 'ideally at a company building for the first time rather than maintaining what already exists'.
SPM JD: 'clear evidence of owning a product area', 'the hard architectural product calls'.
Instincts core finding: thriving hires worked inside operations BEFORE moving into the function they were hired for (Lavanya, Rohan, Sunita, Aditya, Meghna).
Kargo's customers are mid-sized freight forwarders and 3PLs (both JDs). 4 of 5 thriving hires worked at exactly that kind of firm or its CHA/port counterpart.

PM.title: Product Manager
PM.archetype: Lavanya Iyer: 3PL carrier allocation and exceptions → sole PM at a Series A port/logistics SaaS; killed 2 features on usage data; engineering lead: 'She doesn't hedge.'

gates.name: Product experience
gates.rule: product_years >= 1.5 (PM/APM/Product Owner 100%; product decisions owned without a PM 50%). If > 6: PM band capped at Review with flag 'consider_for:SPM'.
gates.grounding: PM JD: '2–4 years of product management experience'. 0.5-year tolerance below; above 6 the person is likely an SPM.

gates.name: Location
gates.rule: Fail only if location_status == explicitly_unwilling. not_stated → pass + flag 'confirm_relocation'.
gates.grounding: PM JD: 'Mumbai-based or willing to relocate. This role is in-office.' Silence on a CV must not reject.

gates.name: Has shipped
gates.rule: P4 level >= 1 (at least one attributable shipped outcome).
gates.grounding: PM JD: 'Evidence that you've shipped things'.

non_negotiables.grounding: 5/5 thriving hires had hands-on ops; PM JD 6-month success: 'spent time inside freight forwarding operations… in the rooms where the work actually happens'.
PM JD: 'You will be the PM — not one of ten'; Lavanya (sole PM) Exceeds vs Vikram (1 of 4 PMs) Meets.
PM JD: 'shipped things, killed things, and learned from both — preferably in short cycles'.
Kargo DNA triad: all 5 thriving hires scored 9/9; the best non-thriving hire (Rahul) scored 5/9.

floors.grounding: Without any ops exposure the maximum score is 72, below the cutoff; the floor makes the rule explicit.

criteria.name: Freight-floor immersion
criteria.grounding: Instinct 1 (5/5 thriving vs 0/3 others). PM JD: 'What does a freight forwarder's morning actually look like? What breaks? What slows them down?'

sub_signals.ops.domain_tier: A = freight forwarding, CHA/customs brokerage, NVOCC, shipping line, port/terminal, air cargo, 3PL. B = warehousing, manufacturing floor, field operations, supply chain planning outside logistics firms. none.
sub_signals.ops.mode: hands_on = personally prepared documents, coordinated carriers/customs, managed exceptions or allocation. desk_adjacent = built software for, sold to, supported, marketed to, or integrated with ops. none.
sub_signals.ops.kargo_surfaces: Subset of [shipment_tracking, documentation, carrier_coordination, customs_clearance, exception_management] the candidate personally performed.
sub_signals.ops.live_crisis: Personally resolved an operational crisis (customs hold, cargo delay, exception) — used for probe selection.

level_rules.3: tier A AND hands_on AND months >= 12 AND >= 2 kargo_surfaces
level_rules.2: tier A AND hands_on (but < 12 months or < 2 surfaces), OR tier B AND hands_on AND months >= 12
level_rules.1: desk_adjacent in tier A/B, OR tier B hands_on < 12 months

criteria.interview_probe: Walk me through a freight forwarder's worst morning that you personally lived through. What broke, who did you call, and what did you change afterwards?

criteria.name: Builds the missing thing, and it spreads
criteria.grounding: Instinct 2 (Rohan's Excel tracker adopted in 2 weeks; Lavanya's dashboard adopted by 2 regional teams; Sunita's weekend workflow kept permanently). PM JD: 'no PM handbook, no design system, no sprint template. You'll build those.'

sub_signals.builds[]: Each: unprompted (bool), gap_type (operational | functional_process | practice_standard), adoption_scope (self | own_team | cross_team | org_standard | customers), permanent (bool), measurable_effect (bool).

level_rules.3: any build that is unprompted AND gap_type == operational AND (adoption cross_team/org_standard/customers OR permanent)
level_rules.2: any build that is unprompted AND adopted by own_team or wider; OR an assigned operational build adopted wider
level_rules.1: any build or improvement at all

criteria.interview_probe: What did you build that nobody asked you to build? How did other teams end up using it?

criteria.name: Sole ownership, no product layer above
criteria.grounding: Instinct 3. PM JD: 'You will be the PM — not one of ten', 'Comfort operating without structure', reports directly to Arjun.

sub_signals.ownership.sole_owner: Sole PM/owner of the product or area with no peer PMs making calls on it.
sub_signals.ownership.owned_incident_to_closure: Personally owned an incident, outage or crisis end to end.
sub_signals.ownership.team_framed_only: Every achievement framed as a team member.

level_rules.2: (layer_above == none OR sole_owner), OR (area_owner AND owned_incident_to_closure)

criteria.interview_probe: Tell me about a product call you made that nobody could overrule. Would you make it again?

criteria.name: Ships and kills on evidence, in short cycles
criteria.grounding: Instinct 5 + PM JD verbatim: 'shipped things, killed things, and learned from both — preferably in short cycles'. PM JD 6-month success: 'two features that customers use without being asked to'.

sub_signals.shipping.killed_or_reversed: Killed or reversed their own work based on evidence

criteria.interview_probe: What's something you shipped that you later killed? What told you, and how fast?

criteria.name: 0→1 building
criteria.grounding: Instinct 4. PM JD: 'a company building for the first time rather than maintaining', 'building a product function from scratch'.

sub_signals.environment.best_stage: early (seed/Series A/<150 people) | independent | mid (Series B+/150–1000) | large (1000+)
sub_signals.environment.first_of_kind: Built the first version of a product, function, process or document at the company

level_rules.2: best_stage in (early, independent), OR (mid AND first_of_kind)

criteria.interview_probe: What did you build from nothing that a bigger company would have handed you on day one?

criteria.name: Discovery with operations users
criteria.grounding: PM JD: 'Customer discovery — … from the people who use it daily'; 'not just over calls, but in the rooms where the work actually happens'. Lavanya's discovery with freight forwarders cut one account's tickets by 60%.

sub_signals.discovery.method: none | secondhand (tickets, analytics, synthesis for others) | interviews | on_site
sub_signals.discovery.users_are_ops: Users interviewed are operations staff (forwarders, carriers, warehouse, field ops)
sub_signals.discovery.changed_build: The finding changed what got built
sub_signals.discovery.quantified_effect: The change had a measured effect

level_rules.3: method in (interviews, on_site) AND users_are_ops AND changed_build AND quantified_effect
level_rules.2: method in (interviews, on_site) AND (changed_build OR users_are_ops)

criteria.interview_probe: Tell me about a discovery session with operations users that changed your roadmap. What did you see that data hadn't shown you?

criteria.name: Engineering knows what's coming three sprints out
criteria.grounding: PM JD: 'The engineering team knows what they are building three sprints out'; 'define what gets built, in what order, and why'.

sub_signals.eng_cadence.signal: none | specs_handoff | direct_scope (worked directly with engineering on scope/sequencing) | owns_rhythm (set the roadmap/prioritisation cadence engineering runs on)

criteria.interview_probe: Three urgent things land in the same sprint. How do you decide, and how does engineering find out?

criteria.name: Built for Kargo's core surfaces
criteria.grounding: PM JD 'What You'll Own': shipment tracking, documentation workflows, and real-time status visibility for freight forwarders.

level_rules.3: customer_type == logistics AND any of tracking_visibility / documentation_workflows / carrier_coordination_scheduling
level_rules.2: customer_type == logistics, OR (customer_type == ops_heavy_b2b AND any surface)

criteria.interview_probe: If you owned shipment tracking at Kargo, what's the first thing you'd want to see our users do in it?

SPM.title: Senior Product Manager
SPM.archetype: Rohan Desai: 32 months as CHA operations executive at JNPT → lead engineer who owned a freight platform's data-vendor migration and translated field requirements 'without a product layer'. There is no senior PM among past hires; this is the closest pattern.

gates.name: Product-ownership experience
gates.rule: product_years >= 4.5 (PM/Product Owner 100%; product decisions owned without a PM 50%). Below → Not shortlisted for SPM, evaluate for PM. Above 10 → pass + flag 'check_level_fit'.
gates.grounding: SPM JD: '5–8 years of product management experience'. 50% credit reflects Rohan's path.

gates.name: Location
gates.grounding: SPM JD: 'Mumbai-based or willing to relocate'.

gates.name: Has owned a product area
gates.grounding: SPM JD: 'clear evidence of owning a product area without a layer of senior PMs above you'.

gates.name: Integration or platform exposure
gates.grounding: SPM JD: owns 'the integration and data layer of Kargo's platform'.

non_negotiables.grounding: SPM JD: ops familiarity is 'a genuine advantage here, not a nice-to-have'; 5/5 thriving hires.
SPM JD: 'no committee that approves product decisions'; 'consequences we will feel two years from now'.
SPM JD 6-month success: 'an integration roadmap… engineering, sales, and Arjun all agree on'.
Kargo DNA triad, same logic as PM.

floors.grounding: No ops exposure at all contradicts the pattern behind every thriving hire.

criteria.name: Freight-floor immersion, including the systems
criteria.grounding: Instinct 1. SPM JD: 'Familiarity with how operations-heavy industries work at ground level… a genuine advantage'; integrations must work inside 'the freight management tools our customers already operate'.

sub_signals.ops.systems_hands_on: Operational systems personally used: CargoWise, ICEGATE/customs EDI, TMS, port or carrier portals, ERP.

level_rules.3: P1-level-3 conditions AND (>= 1 systems_hands_on OR >= 3 kargo_surfaces)
level_rules.2: P1-level-3 conditions without systems, OR P1-level-2 conditions

criteria.interview_probe: Which system our customers run on have you watched fail in real life, and what did people on the floor do when it failed?

criteria.name: Consequential calls, no layer above
criteria.grounding: Instinct 3. SPM JD: 'owning a product area without a layer of senior PMs above you making the calls'; 'make calls in ambiguous situations and live with the consequences'.

sub_signals.decisions.irreversibility: none | low | medium | high (architecture, vendor, platform, data model, migration)
sub_signals.decisions.lived_with_consequence: Reports the outcome of their own call

level_rules.3: final_decider AND irreversibility == high AND lived_with_consequence
level_rules.2: final_decider AND irreversibility in (medium, high), OR (irreversibility == high AND lived_with_consequence)

criteria.interview_probe: What's the hardest-to-reverse product decision you've made? What would have told you it was wrong?

criteria.name: Sets standards that others adopt
criteria.grounding: Instinct 2 (senior form: Rohan's code review and on-call cut P1 incidents 40%). SPM JD: 'The product function has clearer standards for what good PM work looks like, because you have demonstrated it.'

level_rules.3: any build that is unprompted AND (adoption cross_team/org_standard/customers OR permanent) AND measurable_effect
level_rules.2: any build that is unprompted AND adopted by own_team or wider

criteria.interview_probe: What standard for good work have you set that people still follow after you left?

criteria.name: Owns the integration and data layer
criteria.grounding: SPM JD: 'how we connect with carrier systems, port portals, ERP environments, and the freight management tools our customers already operate'.

sub_signals.integration.targets: Subset of [carrier_systems, port_customs_portals, erp, fms_tms, other_3p_api]
sub_signals.integration.owned_migration_or_data_laye: Owned a vendor/data-layer migration or the data layer itself

level_rules.3: role == owner AND any logistics target (carrier_systems/port_customs_portals/erp/fms_tms) AND (external_system_count >= 2 OR owned_migration_or_data_layer)
level_rules.2: role == owner, OR (role == contributor AND logistics target AND external_system_count >= 2)

criteria.interview_probe: Tell me about an integration you chose not to build. What did you do instead, and what did it cost?

criteria.name: Build / configure / stay-away judgement and reliability
criteria.grounding: SPM JD: 'what we build, what we configure, what we stay away from'; 'reliability and data quality standards that freight forwarders can stake their operations on'.

sub_signals.architecture.explicit_build_configure_av: Explicitly describes choosing build vs configure vs avoid
sub_signals.architecture.reliability_metric: Owns a reliability metric (uptime, incidents, lag, data loss)

level_rules.3: explicit_build_configure_avoid AND (reliability_metric OR data_quality_standard) AND role == owner
level_rules.2: role == owner AND (reliability_metric OR data_quality_standard), OR explicit_build_configure_avoid

criteria.interview_probe: Where did you draw the line between building, configuring and refusing? Who disagreed?

criteria.name: Integrations that unlock revenue
criteria.grounding: SPM JD 6-month success: 'At least one major integration has shipped that opened a new customer segment or unblocked a stalled deal'; 'across sales, engineering, and customer operations'.

sub_signals.commercial.functions_worked_with: Subset of [sales, engineering, operations, customer_success, customers]

criteria.interview_probe: Tell me about a deal that closed because of something you built. How did you learn it was blocking?

criteria.name: Environments where the rules weren't written
criteria.grounding: Instinct 4. SPM JD: 'Time spent at an early-stage company, or… environments where the rules were not written yet'.
criteria.interview_probe: What rules did you have to write in your last role that didn't exist when you joined?

criteria.name: Candour: lives with and learns from calls
criteria.grounding: Instinct 5 (weakest signal, 2/5 thriving). SPM JD: 'live with the consequences'; roadmap that 'has not changed three times in six weeks'.
criteria.interview_probe: Tell me about a call you got wrong. What did you change afterwards?

routing.rule: If the applied-role band is below Shortlist and the other-role band is Shortlist or Priority, add flag 'consider_for:<other>'. If the applied band was Not shortlisted, raise it to Review. Never auto-reject someone who clears the other role's bar.
routing.grounding: Components Map: 'Scores candidate against PM and SPM rubrics (both roles)'.

email_policy.priority_shortlist: Interview invite; propose slots within 5 working days.
email_policy.not_shortlisted: Warm, role-specific rejection. Never mention scores, criteria, penalties or the instincts.
email_policy.send: Only via Resend, only when Arjun clicks send.
